investigator_findings.root_cause:
src/cochem_pipeline/coding.py:204-218 (read_workspace) gets each entry's metadata from os.scandir's DirEntry.stat(follow_symlinks=False) at line 210. It then refuses any file whose st_nlink != 1 at line 217. On Windows, DirEntry.stat is built from FindFirstFile/FindNextFile directory data, and st_nlink, st_ino and st_dev are always 0 there. Python documents this under os.DirEntry.stat: "always set to zero. Call os.stat() to get these attributes." So every ordinary file fails the check with 'Worker created a non-regular or hard-linked file'.

read_workspace runs right after the native CLI returns successfully, for every native coding kind (coding.py:440-445). That includes CODE_PLAN, the first stage. So every coding workflow fails at its first native stage, after the inference has already been spent. It runs again after the controller applies a CODE_EDIT (coding.py:467).

The installed r4 package has the same code: lines 199-227 match byte for byte, with the defect at installed coding.py:210.

This is the only DirEntry.stat use anywhere in src/. Every other link-count, inode or device check goes through Path.stat/Path.lstat/os.fstat, which return real values on Windows.

The tests missed it for three reasons:
- The only test that touches read_workspace (pipeline_tests/test_coding_boundaries.py:129-137) checks only the refusal. On Windows it passes because everything is refused.
- No test calls read_workspace on an ordinary file on any platform.
- All CodingFixture-based coding tests skip on Windows unless the run is SYSTEM.

Minimal fix (required). Keep the os.scandir walk and the DirEntry reparse refusal; take link count, size and type from os.lstat per entry. Replace lines 210-219 with:

    listed=item.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
    if stat.S_ISLNK(listed.st_mode) or getattr(listed,'st_file_attributes',0)&0x400:
        raise ValueError('Worker created a symbolic link or reparse point')
    # os.DirEntry.stat() reports st_nlink/st_ino/st_dev as 0 on Windows; os.lstat
    # opens the entry without following links and returns the real NTFS link count.
    metadata=os.lstat(item.path)
    if stat.S_ISLNK(metadata.st_mode) or getattr(metadata,'st_file_attributes',0)&0x400:
        raise ValueError('Worker created a symbolic link or reparse point')

        raise ValueError('Worker workspace entry changed while being inventoried')
    name=validate_source_path(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
    if stat.S_ISDIR(metadata.st_mode):

    size=metadata.st_size

investigator_findings.root_cause: The mechanism is established; the specific cause for job 339ade14 is not. Job 339ade14f7ee44639176a1d8e9c61e14 (CHAPTER_DRAFT, workflow 0213cc0c4da342faa1b9317e4a2552ea, routed to claude:claude-haiku-4-5 after the Gemini candidate was skipped for compatibility, bound to slot6) failed three times. Each attempt lasted about 12 s (12.6, 11.7 and 11.5 s), against 24-58 s for the sibling haiku chapters that succeeded on other slots in the same minute. Every failure was ProviderFailure('code'). In the installed r4 code that category can only come from the inference step, after the controller's own per-attempt checks had passed. Those checks are the Claude --help policy probe, which would raise 'compatibility', and `claude ... auth status --json` in the slot6 profile, which would raise 'auth' (or 'compatibility' for the cache report). So 'code' means one of two things. Either the Claude CLI exited nonzero without any recognised native failure envelope (worker.py:862-863), or it emitted a result record with is_error=true whose cause sits only in its `result` text, which failures.py never inspects, so it falls back to 'code' (failures.py:165-173, 196-209). I checked this against the installed r4 failures.py: Claude result envelopes whose text is 'API Error: 401 ...', 'Invalid API key', 'API Error: 529 ...' or 'API Error: 429 ...' all classify as ('code', None). Because 'code' is not an availability category, it counted against the job's failure budget on the same slot-bound route instead of placing a hold and rerouting. The job hit the three-failure poison pill in 37 s. The real diagnosis exists only in SYSTEM-only per-attempt logs under C:\ProgramData\CoChemPipeline427\private\attempts\<attempt_id>\ (auth.out, auth.err, stdout.log, stderr.log). The public API redacts attempt_id, the native exit code is never recorded for a failed attempt, and the job and slot6 are confounded because a chapter stays bound to its first slot. One hypothesis is ruled out for 22:17-22:18: an explicitly logged-out slot6 session, which would have produced category 'auth'. Five remain open until the logs are copied: (H1) a server-side expired or revoked Claude token while local credentials still report loggedIn; (H2) a rate limit or overload reported only in result text; (H3) a job-specific API rejection or refusal; (H4) a slot6-local CLI crash (profile, config or RAM-disk project cache); (H5) any other nonzero exit with no JSON. The 2026-10-08 status receipts show slot6 Claude logged in at 20:47 and slot6 Codex logged in at 20:39.
